public_rationale: The records establish real reliability problems, including limitations acknowledged before this incident. They also record restored normal operation. Neither fact settles whether generative AI systems had never been stable. Supporting that sweeping statement from selected failures would overstate the evidence; rejecting it from isolated successes would do the same.
limitations: Stable has an ordinary meaning, but its boundary is not specified.
The evidence concerns particular models and episodes rather than the entire history of generative AI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI systems have never been stable.

statement.excerpt: The reality, though is that these systems have never been been stable.

our_interpretation: In context, these systems means generative AI systems, especially conversational language models.
The ordinary reading of stable is reliably coherent and dependable in ordinary operation. It does not require identical answers or flawless performance.
Never makes this a claim about the systems' history through publication. No starting date is supplied, so the historical start remains unspecified.
Individual incidents can establish failures but cannot alone establish that the whole class never achieved stable operation.
criteria.support_condition: Broad historical evidence establishes persistent operational unreliability across the relevant systems, sufficient to support the claim that stable operation had never been achieved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible longitudinal evidence demonstrates sustained, reliably coherent operation by relevant systems under representative ordinary use before publication.
